title: [observability] A pause is a human intervention: the owner's mission.paused counts, and its release as a resume, on the Home card, the Fleet page and Core lines alike (A22, part 3 of 100/103/102)
prompt:
Read the view `spawn_interventions` (crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql) and crates/spawn-postgres/src/experience.rs (`INTERVENTIONS`: the answer of `/api/interventions`, its items' `line`).

The problem (cc-astra A22, HIGH; part 3 of 100/103/102). Objectives 100 and 103 make Core lines and the Fleet page read the Home card's one definition of a human intervention (`spawn_interventions`). That definition still leaves out the owner's hold on a mission: `mission.paused`, which only the owner may record (crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs), and its release `mission.unpaused`. A pause is a person stepping in; while it is missing, a fleet the owner keeps pausing reads as running without anyone.

Required behaviour.
- `spawn_interventions` counts a `mission.paused` record (with an integer `id`) as kind `pause` (mission_id its id), and a `mission.unpaused` record as kind `resume` (the owner releasing the hold, as `mission.resumed` is), at the record's time. Its columns are unchanged (the view may only append; check-schema-upgrade must pass).
- `/api/interventions` items of kind `pause` have the line "paused mission #<id>"; a released pause reads "resumed mission #<id>" like any resume. `by_kind` carries `pause` when one is counted (answer() counts each kind it sees).
- Because the Home card, the Fleet page (`/api/fleet` health.human_per_agent_hour, objective 103) and Core lines (`observability.interventions_per_agent_hour`, objective 100) all read that view, all three move with it and stay equal; nothing else of theirs changes.
- The hints that list the kinds (web/src/components/fleet/Interventions.tsx `HINT` and HealthStrip.tsx `HUMAN_RATE_HINT`) name a pause; docs/fleet-architecture.md's `spawn_interventions` row names both new records.

Files (expected; after 100 and 103, which this one builds on; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (the view only), crates/spawn-postgres/src/experience.rs (the line), web/src/components/fleet/Interventions.tsx and web/src/components/fleet/HealthStrip.tsx (the hint text only), docs/fleet-architecture.md (the view's row), crates/spawn-postgres/tests/experience.rs (the oracle view of the_window_read_gives_the_views_rows_of_every_window, ORACLE: its resume branch widened the same way, so the window read and the oracle still agree row for row). The view's command and resume branches are as rev-f's interventions fix leaves them (each kind's time a column of its base scan); 102 only widens the resume branch's type filter, which stays windowed by spawn_events_control_record_type. Keep it small (well under 40 lines). The fixed kind lists that zero-fill by_kind (scorecard/interventions.rs KINDS, scorecard/fleet.rs, scorecard.rs, measure.rs INTERVENTIONS) and the autonomy dimension are 102b's, later.

Polled-read cost: none added; the resume branch reads the window's control records of its types by spawn_events_control_record_type, and the two added types are read the same way. Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/102.sh. It seeds 7 agent-hours, mission 1 paused 6 h ago and released 3 h ago, and mission 2 paused 30 h ago, and reads /api/interventions (24h and 7d), /api/fleet and /api/core-lines: the card counts the pause and its release (total 2, pause 1, resume 1, 0.286, items "resumed mission #1" then "paused mission #1"; 7 days 3, 0.429), and the Fleet page and Core lines read the same 0.286. 100, 103, 049, 017, 043, 088, 099, 092, 084, 089, 090, check-schema-upgrade and `cargo test -p spawn-postgres --test experience` must still pass.
